statement.excerpt: It’s inevitable, at this point, that both Anthropic and OpenAI’s revenue growth slows, if only because both of them have only got this far through a combination of subsidized subscriptions and companies burning millions on token-maxxing initiatives that will have petered out by the end of the year.

from_speaker: both Anthropic and OpenAI’s revenue growth slows
subsidized subscriptions and companies burning millions on token-maxxing initiatives
will have petered out by the end of the year
our_interpretation: Two parts. (a) The revenue growth rate of each company, OpenAI and Anthropic, will slow. Measured separately for each, as sequential or year-over-year growth falling from its recent pace. (b) Corporate token-maxxing spending will have petered out by the end of 2026.

'By the end of the year' attaches to the petering-out of token-maxxing. The slowdown itself has no stated deadline, but in context it follows from that petering-out, so it is checked over the same window, at the earliest after year-end data.
The causal 'if only because' explanation is not scored separately; it cannot be isolated from public data.
criteria.support_condition: Reported revenue for both OpenAI and Anthropic shows a clear slowdown in growth by or around the end of 2026, along with evidence that corporate token-maxxing spending has faded.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Through the end of 2026, at least one of the two companies shows steady or accelerating revenue growth, or token-maxxing spending continues unabated.
